project.name: Ecclesgreig
project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Full sequential audit. The local HES imports found one listed building and retained all three NRHE records. Three pins have defensible dates; the period-unassigned steading remains map-hidden. Ecclesgreig House is private and not open to the public. No qualifying See, cafe-led Eat, named trail, picnic place, public parking or public toilet was verified inside the strict boundary. St Cyrus attractions and the Mearns Coast Treasure Trail are not transferred to this locality.

features.shortDescription: ECCLESGREIG HOUSE INCLUDING TERRACES, STEPS, AND GRADEN ORNAMENTS
features.reviewNotes: The HES designation describes Henry Edmund Goodridge's 1844 reconstruction. The date is stored in metadata and not appended to the map label.
features.fullDescription: Henry Edmund Goodridge (of Bath, Somerset) 1844, evidently complete reconstruction of earlier house. Jacobean, 2-storey, coursers, symmetrical SE front, 3-storey central division with 2-storey rectangular bay, crowstepped gable and flanking turrets; 2-window either side, upper windows corbelled out with shaped gables, slim angle turrets; NE entrance front has 3-storey and attic battlemented porte- cochere tower, SW front curious square tower broached to circular at top. Idiosyncratic detail, shaped gablets and tall-spired roofs. Extensive pierced balustrades to garden terraces, with finials, numerous garden ornaments.
